sara_dev: Heads up — CI on main turned red right after the deps bump PR (merged ~30m ago). Integration job `linux-integ` failing on wheel build step for `fastparse` with an ImportError in our tests.

nate_build: link to the job?

sara_dev: https://ci.company/2348004/job/9876 — log excerpt: ```
ERROR: Exception in test_setup
ImportError: cannot import name 'TokenizerV2' from 'fastparse' (/opt/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/fastparse/__init__.py)
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'keep_case'
```

ci-bot: CircleCI job linux-integ #9876 failed (exit-code 1) — see above. :warning:

zahid: hmm, TokenizerV2 sounds like a breaking change in fastparse 2.x. Which version did the lock pick up?

sara_dev: our poetry.lock lists `fastparse 2.0.0` under transitive via `text-utils -> token-tools`. The previous green build had `fastparse 1.9.4`.

maria_pr: can someone try a quick local reproduce? `pipx` or venv is fine. If it's a breaking API, short-term fix = pin `fastparse==1.9.4` in constraints while we patch callers.

eli: I'll try a local reproduce on macos (same python 3.10). If it's a transitive bump we should bisect the lockfile commit to find which dep bumped it.

nate_build: Could also be platform wheel difference — 2.0 might ship different binary wheel that exposes different symbols. Try `pip install fastparse==2.0.0` and run the failing test file directly: `pytest tests/integration/test_tokenizer.py::test_tokenizer_init -q`.

zahid: to bisect quickly: 
```
# from repo root
git checkout main~6  # start a few commits back
git bisect start --term-old=GOOD --term-new=BAD
# mark known bad (current main) and known good commit hash
git bisect good <good-hash>
git bisect bad main
# then run the small script to check for fastparse version in lock
python tools/check_lock_fastparse.py || git bisect bad
# make the script exit 0 when lock had 1.9.4
```
(we have a tiny helper `tools/check_lock_fastparse.py` that prints the fastparse version out of poetry.lock)

sara_dev: running reproduce now on a Linux container.

eli: quick note — I hit the same TypeError locally after `pip install fastparse==2.0.0`. Looks like the initializer signature changed in 2.x and our wrapper is passing `keep_case`.

maria_pr: can we patch our wrapper to accept the param for backward compat, then do a tiny release? That avoids pinning if upstream already fixed docs but not compat.

nate_build: Also worth checking if any other packages changed API; but bisect will tell us the exact commit that updated token-tools->fastparse.

sara_dev: CI container reproduce: ```
$ docker run -it --rm python:3.10-bullseye bash
# inside container
pip install poetry==1.5.1
poetry install --no-dev
pytest tests/integration/test_tokenizer.py::test_tokenizer_init -q
```
It fails the same.

zahid: if bisect shows the bump commit, we can either revert that lockfile update, pin fastparse in our constraints, or add wrapper compatibility. For immediate unblocking, pinning in `pyproject.toml` constraints is fastest.

ci-bot: Re-run requested by sara_dev on linux-integ #9876 — queued. :white_check_mark:

sara_dev: re-run passed on linux-integ with cached artifacts? Wait — the rerun shows different failure: now `s3upload` step errors with `InvalidSeekError` (weird). Might be flaky infra.

eli: rerun may be hiding the original wheel failure (cache). Need a clean build: `CIRCLECI_REBUILD=full` or clear caches.

nate_build: I'll trigger a hard rebuild and meanwhile add a short constraints pin to our `constraints/production.txt`: `fastparse==1.9.4` and open a revert PR for the lock bump.

maria_pr: thanks — once the revert or pin PR is up ping me for a quick review. We should also add a CI check that flags transitive major bumps in critical libs.

sara_dev: PR opened: https://git/2348/pr/482 — pins fastparse and adds a note in CHANGELOG. Running CI.

zahid: after pin PR merges, follow-up: create an issue to coordinate with token-tools maintainers to either bump their compatibility or adopt new API.

eli: quick win: add try/except in our wrapper around Tokenizer import to provide clearer error if incompatible. I'll draft it.

sara_dev: awesome, thanks everyone. Will monitor after the pin PR. :rocket:
